taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Azure managed identity delegation through a workload-controlled operation
controls.source_trace: Trace who can cause the workload to act and which identity/resource scope it uses. A platform identity endpoint is not independently an authorization flaw.
controls.implementation_branch: Map the caller-controlled operation to the workload identity it uses and the exact resource action. Access to a metadata endpoint inside an owned workload is not itself a confused-deputy finding. Determine which identities the workload can select and whether its public API constrains destination, tenant and action before using the ambient identity.
controls.operational_method: Record system-assigned versus user-assigned identity, the actual token endpoint and selector supported by that workload, and who can attach/select identities. Follow a caller input through endpoint selection into the token resource/audience and final Azure action. In a stub, expose two identity handles with disjoint permissions and verify that caller-controlled identity selection cannot borrow the stronger one. Endpoint reachability alone does not establish an unauthorized delegated operation.
controls.controlled_verification: Use an owned workload fixture and synthetic resource; compare its intended operation with a caller-selected out-of-policy resource/action.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Obtaining identity metadata or a correctly scoped denied token does not prove broader Azure resource access.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Constrain workload delegation and assigned permissions, then verify legitimate calls and resource/audience rejection.
